name: Barthel Index
description: "The Barthel Index (BI; Mahoney & Barthel, 1965) was developed as a measure of disability in people whose impairment interfered with independent use of their limbs. The BI includes the 10 activities of daily living (self-care and mobility) that are commonly included in activities of daily living (ADL) checklists and physical function instruments. A number of studies (e.g., Loewen & Anderson, 1988) have indicated excellent intra- and interrater reliability for the BI."
description_reference: https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/t02366-000
plain-language_description: A tool to rank a patient's independence in 10 areas of daily living, such as feeding, bathing, dressing and mobility: https://www.sralab.org/sites/default/files/downloads/2025-02/Barthel%20Index.pdf

name: Glasgow Coma Score
description: "A clinical scale has been evolved for assessing the depth and duration of impaired consciousness and coma. Three aspects of behaviour are independently measured—motor responsiveness, verbal performance, and eye opening. These can be evaluated consistently by doctors and nurses and recorded on a simple chart which has proved practical both in a neurosurgical unit and in a general hospital. The scale facilitates consultations between general and special units in cases of recent brain damage, and is useful also in defining the duration of prolonged coma."
description_reference:
Teasdale G, Jennett B
ASSESSMENT OF COMA AND IMPAIRED CONSCIOUSNESS
The Lancet, 304, 81-84

name: Glasgow Outcome Scale
description: "A five-point scale is described—death, persistent vegetative state, severe disability, moderate disability, and good recovery. Duration as well as intensity of disability should be included in an index of ill-health; this applies particularly after head injury, because many disabled survivors are young."
description_reference: Jennett, Bryan, and Michael Bond. “ASSESSMENT OF OUTCOME AFTER SEVERE BRAIN DAMAGE: A Practical Scale.” The Lancet (British Edition), vol. 305, no. 7905, March 1975, pp. 480–84, https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(75)92830-5.

name: Glasgow Outcome Scale extended
description: "To increase the sensitivity of the GOS, Jennett and colleagues later suggested that categories of outcome could be divided into upper and lower bands to create an expanded 8-point scale." The 8 categories are the following: dead, vegetative state, lower severe disability, upper severe disability, Lower moderate disability, upper moderate disability, lower good recovery, and upper good recovery
description_reference: Wilson L, Boase K, Nelson LD, et al. A Manual for the Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended Interview. Journal of Neurotrauma. 2021;38(17):2435-2446. doi:10.1089/neu.2020.7527

name: Modified Rankin Scale
description: "The modified Rankin Scale (mRS) is a single-item, global outcome rating scale that was developed to measure the degree of disability or dependence in the daily activities of people who have suffered from stroke or other neurological disorders...The mRS has a range between 0 and 6, where a score of 0 is ‘no symptoms at all’ and a score of 6 is ‘dead’; there are no subscales."
description_reference: Haggag, Hammazah, and Carol Hodgson. “Clinimetrics: Modified Rankin Scale (mRS).” Journal of Physiotherapy, vol. 68, no. 4, October 2022, pp. 281–281, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jphys.2022.05.017.

name: National Institute of Health Stroke Scale
description: "The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) is a 15-item impairment scale used to measure stroke severity...The NIHSS includes the following domains: level of consciousness, eye movements, integrity of visual fields, facial movements, arm and leg muscle strength, sensation, coordination, language, speech and neglect. Each impairment is scored on an ordinal scale ranging from 0 to 2, 0 to 3, or 0 to 4. Item scores are summed to a total score ranging from 0 to 42 (the higher the score, the more severe the stroke)."
description_reference: Kwah, Li Khim, and Joanna Diong. “National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS).” Journal of Physiotherapy [Netherlands], vol. 60, no. 1, March 2014, pp. 61–61, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jphys.2013.12.012.

name: Subarachnoid Haemorrhage Outcome Tool
description: "The final SAHOT included 56 items dealing with cognitive, physical, and behavioural/psychological consequences of subarachnoid haemorrhage... The SAHOT offers the first subarachnoid haemorrhage-specific scientifically robust outcome measure with potential utility in neurovascular clinical services and research studies."
description_reference: Pace, Adrian, et al. “A Subarachnoid Haemorrhage-Specific Outcome Tool.” Brain (London, England : 1878) [England], vol. 141, no. 4, April 2018, pp. 1111–21, https://doi.org/10.1093/brain/awy003.

name: Functional Status Examination
description: "The Functional Status Examination (FSE) is a new measure designed to evaluate change in activities of everyday life as a function of an event or illness, including traumatic brain injury. The measure covers physical, social, and psychological domains. The FSE is based on a structured interview and includes levels of functioning that accommodate the full spectrum of possible outcomes, from death through recovery to preinjury functioning."
description_reference: Dikmen S, Machamer J, Miller B, Doctor J, Temkin N. Functional Status Examination: A New Instrument for Assessing Outcome in Traumatic Brain Injury. Journal of Neurotrauma. 2001;18(2):127-140. doi:10.1089/08977150150502578

name: Karnofsky Performance Status Scale
description: "The Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) is a widely used method to assess the functional status of a patient... The KPS describes a patient’s functional status as a comprehensive 11-point scale correlating to percentage values ranging from 100% (no evidence of disease, no symptoms) to 0% (death)."
description_reference: Péus, Dominik, et al. “Appraisal of the Karnofsky Performance Status and Proposal of a Simple Algorithmic System for Its Evaluation.” BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making [London], vol. 13, no. 1, no. 72, July 2013, https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6947-13-72.

name: World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies (WFNS) Scale
description: "GCS is also the main component of the World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies (WFNS) classification. In patients with SAH, WFNS classification is used to measure clinical severity on presentation. WFNS classification was developed in 1988 and started as a scale that was largely based upon consensus among experts. It has been shown to have good discriminatory ability for prognostication of SAH. Although in practice it is usually combined with an imaging scale (such as the Fisher Grade), WFNS scale itself quantifies severity on the basis of clinical presentation, but not on radiological."
description_reference: Behrouz, Réza, and Asma Zakaria. “Can the World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies Classification Accurately Predict Outcomes in Intracerebral Hemorrhage?.” Journal of vascular and interventional neurology vol. 8,2 (2015): 9-12.

name: AMC Linear Disability Score
description: "The AMC Linear Disability Score (ALDS) project aims to construct an item bank to measure the functional status of patients with a broad range of stable, chronic diseases"
description_reference: Holman, Rebecca, et al. “Constructing an Item Bank Using Item Response Theory: The AMC Linear Disability Score Project.” Health Services and Outcomes Research Methodology [Dordrecht], vol. 4, no. 1, March 2003, pp. 19–33, https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1025824810390.

name: Rivermead concussion instrument
description: "The Rivermead PCS Questionnaire (RPQ) is another self-report measure of PCS [ost-concussion symptoms], originally developed as a measure of severity of symptoms following MTBI [mild traumatic brain injury]. It consists of 16 post-concussion symptoms including headaches, dizziness, nausea/vomiting, noise sensitivity, sleep disturbance, fatigue, irritability, feeling depressed/tearful, feeling frustrated/impatient, forgetfulness, poor concentration, taking longer to think, blurred vision, light sensitivity, double vision and restlessnesss. For each symptom, individuals are asked to rate the degree (on a scale of 0 to 4) to which it has been absent or a mild, moderate or severe problem over the previous 24 hours compared with premorbid levels. Ratings of ‘‘no more of a problem’’ compared with pre-injury levels are also available (corresponding to item values of 1), but are not typically added when calculating the overall total score."
description_reference: Potter, Seb, et al. “The Rivermead Post Concussion Symptoms Questionnaire: A Confirmatory Factor Analysis: A Confirmatory Factor Analysis.” Journal of Neurology [Berlin], vol. 253, no. 12, December 2006, pp. 1603–14, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00415-006-0275-z.

name: Full Outline of Un-Responsiveness Score
description: "The Full Outline of Un-Responsiveness Score (FOURs) is a scale for clinical assessment of consciousness that was introduced to overcome disadvantages of the widely accepted Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)... It involves 4 components: eye response, motor response (which includes gesturing in an attempt to replace verbal response), brainstem reflexes and breathing pattern."
description_reference: Anestis, Dimitrios M., et al. “The Current Significance of the FOUR Score: A Systematic Review and Critical Analysis of the Literature.” Journal of the Neurological Sciences [Netherlands], vol. 409, no. 116600, February 2020, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jns.2019.116600.

name: Short-Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) Score
description: "[T]he domains of balance and gait are explored also by the Short-Physical Performance Battery (SPPB). This is a widely used scale exploring the reduction of physical performance in older persons, particularly muscle strength of lower extremities, 4-m walking speed at usual pace, and balance. It has the ability of predicting mobility-disability, nursing home and hospital admission. Poor physical performance and balance alterations are among the main causes of falls in older individuals."
description_reference: Lauretani, F., Ticinesi, A., Gionti, L. et al. Short-Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) score is associated with falls in older outpatients. Aging Clin Exp Res 31, 1435–1442 (2019). https://doi.org/10.1007/s40520-018-1082-y

name: Patient Competency Rating Scale
description: "The PCRS is a 30-item self-report questionnaire that asks patients and family members to make independent judgements about the perceived degree of competency the patient demonstrates on various behavioural, cognitive and emotional tasks. Comparison of patient ratings to family member ratings allows for insight into how realistic a patient is in evaluating his/her limitations."
description_reference: Borgaro, Susan R., and George P. Prigatano. “Modification of the Patient Competency Rating Scale for Use on an Acute Neurorehabilitation Unit: The PCRS-NR.” Brain Injury [London], vol. 17, no. 10, October 2003, pp. 847–53, https://doi.org/10.1080/0269905031000089350.

name: 12-Item / 36-Item Short Form Surveys
description:
"The SF-36 includes one multi-item scale that assesses eight health concepts."
"Regression methods were used to select and score 12 items from the Medical Outcomes Study 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36)."
description_reference:
Ware JE Jr, Sherbourne CD. The MOS 36-item short-form health survey (SF-36). I. Conceptual framework and item selection. Med Care. 1992;30(6):473-483. PMID: 1593914. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1593914/

Ware J Jr, Kosinski M, Keller SD. A 12-Item Short-Form Health Survey: construction of scales and preliminary tests of reliability and validity. Med Care. 1996;34(3):220-233. doi:10.1097/00005650-199603000-00003. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8628042/
plain-language_description: The SF-12 and SF-36 questionnaires ask how a person’s health affects physical activity, everyday roles, pain, energy, social life, and emotional well-being. The SF-12 is the shorter version.

name: Canadian Occupational Performance Measure
description: "The COPM is an outcome measure designed for use by occupational therapists to assess client outcomes in the areas of self-care, productivity and leisure."
description_reference: Law M, Baptiste S, McColl M, Opzoomer A, Polatajko H, Pollock N. The Canadian occupational performance measure: an outcome measure for occupational therapy. Can J Occup Ther. 1990;57(2):82-87. doi:10.1177/000841749005700207. PMID: 10104738. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10104738/
plain-language_description: The Canadian Occupational Performance Measure helps a person identify important self-care, productivity, and leisure activities, then rate their performance and satisfaction with that performance.

name: Functional Activities Questionnaire
description: "The Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ) is a collateral-report measure of difficulties in instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs)."
description_reference: González DA, Gonzales MM, Resch ZJ, et al. Comprehensive evaluation of the Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ) and its reliability and validity. Assessment. 2022;29(4):748-763. doi:10.1177/1073191121991215. PMCID: PMC8339133. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8339133/
plain-language_description: The Functional Activities Questionnaire asks a family member or other informant to rate how independently a person manages complex everyday tasks such as finances, shopping, meals, and appointments.

name: Functional Capacity Scale
description: "The scale has 12 markers: ambulation, alimentation, personal hygiene, physiological needs, life functions measurement (GCS), breathing, diagnosis, pre- and post-operative treatment."
description_reference: Ślusarz R, Beuth W, Śniegocki M. Functional Capacity Scale as a new tool for early functional assessment in patients after surgical treatment of intracranial aneurysms. Med Sci Monit. 2012;18(11):CR680-CR686. doi:10.12659/MSM.883547. PMCID: PMC3560615. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3560615/
plain-language_description: The Functional Capacity Scale is a bedside scale that describes how much help a patient needs soon after aneurysm surgery, based on mobility, self-care, neurological status, breathing, and treatment needs.

name: Functional Independence Measure
description: "The Functional Independence Measure (FIM) is an 18-item, 7-level scale developed to uniformly assess severity of patient disability and medical rehabilitation functional outcome."
description_reference: Hamilton BB, Laughlin JA, Fiedler RC, Granger CV. Interrater reliability of the 7-level functional independence measure (FIM). Scand J Rehabil Med. 1994;26(3):115-119. PMID: 7801060. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7801060/
plain-language_description: The Functional Independence Measure rates how much assistance a person needs for self-care, mobility, communication, and basic cognitive tasks.

name: Global Rating of Change
description: "Global Rating of Change Scale involves a single question that measures self-perceived change in health status."
description_reference: Kamper SJ, Maher CG, Mackay G. Global rating of change scales: a review of strengths and weaknesses and considerations for design. J Man Manip Ther. 2009;17(3):163-170. doi:10.1179/jmt.2009.17.3.163. PMID: 20046623. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20046623/ (Also from Sude et al., 2021: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8044055/)
plain-language_description: The Global Rating of Change Scale asks a person whether their condition is better, worse, or unchanged compared with an earlier time, and by how much.

name: Hospital Assessment Scale
description: "Hospital Assessment Scale (HAS), a simplified four-point ordinal scale for in-hospital use."
description_reference: Solodovnikova Y, Son A. How to Simplify In-Hospital Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Outcome: The Hospital Assessment Scale. World Neurosurg. 2025;202:124457. PMID: 40935243. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40935243/
plain-language_description: The Hospital Assessment Scale classifies an in-hospital aSAH outcome into four levels, ranging from no neurological deficit to dependence or death.

name: Lawton Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) Scale
description: "The Lawton Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) Scale assesses a person’s ability to perform tasks such as using a telephone."
description_reference: Graf C. The Lawton instrumental activities of daily living scale. Am J Nurs. 2008;108(4):52-62. doi:10.1097/01.NAJ.0000314810.46029.74. PMID: 18367931. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18367931/ Original instrument: Lawton MP, Brody EM. Assessment of older people: self-maintaining and instrumental activities of daily living. Gerontologist. 1969;9(3):179-186. PMID: 5349366. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/5349366/
plain-language_description: The Lawton Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale checks whether a person can independently manage complex everyday tasks such as shopping, cooking, transportation, medicines, and money.

name: Montreal Cognitive Assessment
description: "The MoCA is a brief cognitive screening tool with high sensitivity and specificity for detecting MCI."
description_reference: Nasreddine ZS, Phillips NA, Bédirian V, et al. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment, MoCA: a brief screening tool for mild cognitive impairment. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2005;53(4):695-699. doi:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2005.53221.x. PMID: 15817019. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15817019/
plain-language_description: The Montreal Cognitive Assessment briefly tests a person’s memory, attention, language, visuospatial skills, and executive thinking; it measures cognition rather than everyday functional independence directly.

name: Occupational Gaps Questionnaire
description: "The Occupational Gaps Questionnaire" measures "a discrepancy between what they want to do and what they actually do."
description_reference:
Eriksson T, Jonsson H, Tham K, Eriksson G. A comparison of perceived occupational gaps between people with stress-related ill health or musculoskeletal pain and a reference group. Scand J Occup Ther. 2012;19(5):411-420. doi:10.3109/11038128.2011.620984. PMID: 22029609. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22029609/

Eriksson G, Tham K, Kottorp A. A cross-diagnostic validation of an instrument measuring participation in everyday occupations: the Occupational Gaps Questionnaire (OGQ). Scand J Occup Ther. 2013;20(2):152-160. doi:10.3109/11038128.2012.749944. PMID: 23216376. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23216376/
plain-language_description: The Occupational Gaps Questionnaire compares the everyday activities a person actually does with the activities they want to do. It identifies an occupational gap when these do not match.

name: Patient Assessment of Own Functioning Inventory
description: "The PAOFI is a tool intended to measure a continuum of self-reported functioning" across memory, language and communication, hand use, sensory-perceptual ability, and higher cognition.
description_reference: Heinsberg LW, Bender CM, Rohay JM, Sherwood PR, Crago EA. Psychometric Properties of the Patient Assessment of Own Functioning Inventory Following Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage. J Nurs Meas. 2020;28(2):205-228. doi:10.1891/JNM-D-18-00117. PMID: 32341171; PMCID: PMC7442614. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7442614/
plain-language_description: The Patient Assessment of Own Functioning Inventory asks a person how often they notice problems with memory, language and communication, hand use, perception, and higher-level thinking in everyday life.

name: Physical Performance Test
description: "The Physical Performance Test (PPT) assesses multiple domains of physical function using observed performance of tasks that simulate activities of daily living."
description_reference: Reuben DB, Siu AL. An objective measure of physical function of elderly outpatients: The Physical Performance Test. J Am Geriatr Soc. 1990;38(10):1105-1112. doi:10.1111/j.1532-5415.1990.tb01373.x. PMID: 2229864. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2229864/
plain-language_description: The Physical Performance Test requires a person to perform practical physical tasks, such as walking, dressing, and picking up an object, while an assessor scores their performance.

name: Return-to-Work CRF
description: The NINDS SAH working group classifies the Return to Work CRF under "Participation Restriction/Return to Work" and recommends it as an exploratory case-report form.
description_reference:
Suarez JI, Sheikh MK, Macdonald RL, et al. Common Data Elements for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms and Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Clinical Research: A National Institute for Neurological Disorders and Stroke and National Library of Medicine Project. Neurocrit Care. 2019;30(Suppl 1):4-19. doi:10.1007/s12028-019-00723-6. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12028-019-00723-6

NINDS CDE Project. Outcomes and Endpoints Working Group Recommendations. The table lists the Return to Work CRF in the Participation Restriction/Return to Work subdomain. https://commondataelements.ninds.nih.gov/sites/nindscde/files/Doc/SAH/F2332_NINDS_CDE_Project_SAH_WG_Summary_Outcomes_Endpoints.pdf
plain-language_description: The Return to Work CRF is a standardized research form that records a person’s work participation after SAH. The form is a data-collection module, not a scored measurement scale.

name: Stroke Impact Scale  (long version)
description: "The Stroke Impact Scale is a 59-item measure examining eight domains of health status: strength, hand function, ADL, mobility, communication, emotions, memory and participation."
description_reference: Duncan PW, Wallace D, Lai SM, Johnson D, Embretson S, Laster LJ. The Stroke Impact Scale Version 2.0: evaluation of reliability, validity, and sensitivity to change. Stroke. 1999;30(10):2131-2140. doi:10.1161/01.STR.30.10.2131. PMID: 10512918. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10512918/
plain-language_description: The Stroke Impact Scale asks a person about strength, hand use, daily activities, mobility, communication, memory, emotions, and participation after stroke.

name: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-III-R
description: "The SCID is a semistructured interview for making the major Axis I DSM-III-R diagnoses."
description_reference: Spitzer RL, Williams JBW, Gibbon M, First MB. The Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-III-R (SCID). I: History, rationale, and description. Arch Gen Psychiatry. 1992;49(8):624-629. doi:10.1001/archpsyc.1992.01820080032005. PMID: 1637252. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1637252/
plain-language_description: The Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-III-R is a clinician-administered interview used to diagnose psychiatric disorders; it fits Mood and Emotion more closely than Functional Outcomes.

name: Unified Neurological Stroke Scale
description: "The Unified Stroke Scale demonstrates reliability and construct and predictive validity, and its use is supported in ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke."
description_reference: Edwards DF, Chen YW, Diringer MN. Unified Neurological Stroke Scale is valid in ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. Stroke. 1995;26(10):1852-1858. doi:10.1161/01.STR.26.10.1852. PMID: 7570738. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7570738/
plain-language_description: The Unified Neurological Stroke Scale rates a person’s neurological impairment after stroke; it may predict later function but does not directly measure everyday independence or participation.

name: Work Limitations Questionnaire
description: The Work Limitations Questionnaire was developed "for measuring the on-the-job impact of chronic health problems and/or treatment (work limitations)."
description_reference: Lerner D, Amick BC 3rd, Rogers WH, Malspeis S, Bungay K, Cynn D. The Work Limitations Questionnaire. Med Care. 2001;39(1):72-85. doi:10.1097/00005650-200101000-00009. PMID: 11176545. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11176545/
plain-language_description: The Work Limitations Questionnaire asks an employed person how health problems affect their time management, physical work, mental and interpersonal demands, and ability to produce the required amount of work.

name: Brain Injury Community Rehabilitation Outcome-39
description: "Construction and validation of a new instrument, the Brain Injury Community Rehabilitation Outcome scales, to assess problems experienced by brain-injured patients living in the community."
description_reference: Powell JH, Beckers K, Greenwood RJ. Measuring progress and outcome in community rehabilitation after brain injury with a new assessment instrument—the BICRO-39 scales. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 1998;79(10):1213-1225. doi:10.1016/S0003-9993(98)90265-9. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0003-9993(98)90265-9
plain-language_description: The Brain Injury Community Rehabilitation Outcome-39 assesses a person’s community life after brain injury, including personal care, mobility, organization, work, social life, psychological functioning, and family relationships.

name: Role Resumption List
description: The Role Resumption List "assesses changes in amount and quality of activities compared with premorbid levels" in work, social relations, leisure activities, and mobility.
description_reference: Spikman JM, Boelen DHE, Lamberts KF, Brouwer WH, Fasotti L. Effects of a multifaceted treatment program for executive dysfunction after acquired brain injury on indications of executive functioning in daily life. J Int Neuropsychol Soc. 2010;16(1):118-129. doi:10.1017/S1355617709991020. PMID: 19900348. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19900348/ Buunk AM, Groen RJM, Veenstra WS, Spikman JM. Leisure and social participation in patients 4-10 years after aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage. Brain Inj. 2015;29(13-14):1589-1596. doi:10.3109/02699052.2015.1073789. PMID: 26362688. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26362688/
plain-language_description: The Role Resumption List uses a structured interview to compare a person’s current work, social relationships, leisure activities, and mobility with their participation before the brain injury.

name: Utrecht Scale for Evaluation of Rehabilitation-Participation
description: "The USER-Participation comprises 31 items in three scales: Frequency, Restrictions and Satisfaction."
description_reference: Post MWM, van der Zee CH, Hennink J, Schafrat CG, Visser-Meily JMA, van Berlekom SB. Validity of the Utrecht Scale for Evaluation of Rehabilitation-Participation. Disabil Rehabil. 2012;34(6):478-485. doi:10.3109/09638288.2011.608148. PMID: 21978031. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21978031/
plain-language_description: The Utrecht Scale for Evaluation of Rehabilitation-Participation asks how often a person participates in work, household, leisure, and social activities, what restrictions they experience, and how satisfied they are.

name: Sickness Impact Profile
description: "The SIP is a questionnaire instrument designed to measure sickness-related behavioral dysfunction” for use as an outcome measure."
description_reference:
Pollard WE, Bobbitt RA, Bergner M, Martin DP, Gilson BS. The Sickness Impact Profile: reliability of a health status measure. Med Care. 1976;14(2):146-155. PMID: 1256107. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1256107/

Bergner M, Bobbitt RA, Pollard WE, Martin DP, Gilson BS. The Sickness Impact Profile: conceptual formulation and methodology for the development of a health status measure. Int J Health Serv. 1976;6(3):393-415. PMID: 955750. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/955750/
plain-language_description: The Sickness Impact Profile asks whether illness has changed a person’s everyday behaviour across activities such as mobility, self-care, work, household tasks, recreation, social interaction, sleep, and communication.

name: PROMIS Physical Function
description: "The final bank consists of 124 PROMIS items covering upper, central, and lower extremity functions and instrumental activities of daily living."
description_reference: Rose M, Bjorner JB, Becker J, et al. The PROMIS Physical Function item bank was calibrated to a standardized metric and shown to improve measurement efficiency. J Clin Epidemiol. 2014;67(5):516-526. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2013.10.024. PMID: 24698295; PMCID: PMC4465404. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24698295/
plain-language_description: PROMIS Physical Function asks a person about their ability to move, use their arms and legs, and carry out physical and instrumental activities of daily living.

name: PROMIS Ability to Participate in Social Roles and Activities
description: The PROMIS item bank "measures social participation across health conditions and disabilities" through a person’s ability to perform usual social roles and activities.
description_reference: van Leeuwen LM, Terwee CB, Luijten MAJ, et al. Proposal to extend the PROMIS item bank v2.0 ‘Ability to Participate in Social Roles and Activities’: item generation and content validity. Qual Life Res. 2020;29(11):3047-3059. doi:10.1007/s11136-020-02540-3. PMCID: PMC7561593. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7561593/
plain-language_description: PROMIS Ability to Participate in Social Roles and Activities asks a person how well they can take part in their usual family, social, work, and community roles.

name: Rancho Los Amigos Cognitive Scale-Revised
description: The Rancho Los Amigos Cognitive Scale-Revised (RLAS-R) is a 10-level observational measure used to characterize cognitive and behavioral recovery following traumatic brain injury. The scale evaluates responsiveness, attention, memory, executive functioning, behavior, and functional independence, providing a framework for monitoring recovery and guiding rehabilitation planning.
description_reference: Hagen, C., Malkmus, D., & Durham, P. (1972). Levels of Cognitive Functioning Scale. Rancho Los Amigos Hospital, Downey, CA
plain-language_description: The Rancho Los Amigos Cognitive Scale-Revised (RLAS-R) is a standardized measure used to describe the cognitive and behavioral recovery of individuals following a traumatic brain injury (TBI) or other severe acquired brain injuries. The scale tracks recovery from coma and severe impairment through increasing levels of awareness, thinking, behavior, and independence.
